name: quit-after-devtools-cycle
description: Matrix D - the one state with recorded evidence of a DROPPED Cmd+Q. Mirrors devtools-close-while-docked's actions exactly, but makes the quit the assertion instead of the liveness window count. On 2026-07-24 that scenario's teardown found the process still alive after Cmd+Q + 2000ms, which is why it deliberately asserts ax_window_count instead - the signal inverts there. Here the app is known to survive the undock (that scenario asserts it), so a FAIL is unambiguously a dropped quit, not a crash.

actions.note: let the space and its single tab render
make Atrium frontmost before any synthetic key
let the DevTools frontend load and dock
toggle DevTools back off - the undock/teardown path that preceded the observed drop
let the detach + focus restore settle
evidence of the post-undock state Cmd+Q is pressed in

assertions.label: devtools-undocked
assertions.note: the undock really happened - without it the quit below would be testing an ordinary window
assertions.desc: the undock must come AFTER a dock. Atrium logs 'devtools pane ... docked=0 bounds=0,0 0x0 hide_inspected=0' at LAUNCH, and the line it logs after a real undock is byte-identical - same pane pointer, same zero bounds - so presence alone was true of an app that never opened DevTools. This assertion once passed while DevTools was completely dead. Ordering is the only thing that separates them.
Cmd+Q quits after a DevTools dock/undock cycle (the 2026-07-24 drop)
